flagged.evidence: "If you call root.render before the root has finished hydrating, React will clear the existing server-rendered HTML content and switch the entire root to client rendering." https://react.dev/reference/react-dom/client/hydrateRoot
flagged.problem: The answer and explanation are correct, but this is a caveat of a low-level React DOM root API. In a Next.js app the framework creates and owns the hydrateRoot root, so app code never calls root.render. It has no bearing on building a Next.js app.

okWithNotes.problem: Minor: on a hydration mismatch React can discard server HTML and client render a subtree, but that is the error path, not what hydration is, so the general statement is still false.

Next.js developers never call hydrateRoot themselves (Next.js does it). The idea that rendered output must match still matters for Next.js hydration errors, so the card is in scope, but it could say 'Hydration' instead of 'hydrateRoot'.
Minor: for dynamic routes prefetching is skipped or only partial (if loading.tsx is present). Because the statement says 'can', it is still true.

The opposite case is weak. The glossary describes dynamic route segments as 'generated from data at request time', and without an array from generateStaticParams the route is dynamically rendered. But 'forces' is still false because generateStaticParams prerenders the segment. The answer and explanation are correct. The cited source only covers the point in passing.
okWithNotes.suggestedFix: Optional: replace the source URL with https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params, which states the claim directly.

okWithNotes.problem: The opposite case is weak. With no Suspense boundary at all, a production build of a static page fails with the 'Missing Suspense boundary with useSearchParams' error. But the statement assumes a boundary exists ('nearest Suspense boundary'). The cacheComponents-off qualifier is narrower than it needs to be, since the page does not limit the rule to either mode. That narrowing is not wrong.

Edge cases that do not break the card: (1) with cacheComponents off, connection() makes the whole route dynamic, which goes beyond 'below that call', so the statement understates the effect but stays true; (2) with Cache Components, the docs now recommend io() over connection() for excluding content from the static shell, but connection() keeps the same behaviour. A route with dynamic = 'force-static' is not covered by the docs, so I did not count it against the card.
